text:
emily: Heads-up: ran into surprising auth behavior in python SDK when running two clients in same process and rotating api keys externally.
rahul: Can you paste a tiny repro? sync/async?
emily: sync client in our sidecar. Minimal: 
```
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']='K1'
client1 = RedwoodClient()
# external rotates env to K2
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']='K2'
resp = client1.embeddings.create(...) # still uses K1
```
kevin: Hmm. If the SDK resolves the env at import/init and caches it on a global provider, that would explain it.
sdk-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/870 (labels: bug, auth)
olivia: Did you try passing api_key explicitly to constructor? That should pin per-client and avoid global caching.
emily: We tried. Passing api_key each time works but our infra rotates keys and writes to env; we prefer to avoid plumbing key through call sites.
rahul: Two actionable things: (1) add an AuthProvider Protocol/typed interface so callers can plug a tiny provider class that reads os.getenv per call; (2) add public client.reload_credentials() to force refresh.
kevin: Agreed. Also a doc section "rotating credentials in long-lived processes" with example provider. For mypy users the Protocol is important.
emily: Workaround I used: small provider object with __call__ that reads env and returns header; pass to client as api_key_provider. Works fine.
sdk-bot: Routing to #eng-sdks (ticket: SDK-870)
rahul: For SDK internals: consider making the default env-backed provider cache for N seconds and allow env_read_strategy="per_call" for opt-in. That balances perf with rotation needs.
kevin: Also add an integration test that creates two clients with different env values and asserts requests use the correct key over time, plus a concurrent-init test.
emily: filing a short PR with test and docs snippet after we land the issue. Saving this thread so others running sidecars see the pattern. :coffee:
